Shamsul Alam, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.

Shankar Chandra Das and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Kalachand Das ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Babu Tufan Das, the predecessor of the plaintiff appellant-petitioner being plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 235 of 1981 in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) 2nd court at Barisal against the defendant-opposite party for khan possession by evicting the defendant from the suit but as described in the schedule to the plaint and subsequently on transfer of the suit to the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal, it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 395 of 1984. The case of the plaintiff is that the plaintiff is the owner of 0.09 decimal of land of RS plot No. 2048 by pattan taken in 1359 BS from the previous owner Sukumar Sen and others. This land was wrongly recorded in the khatian in the name of the previous owner and so, the plaintiff Tufan Das filed a suit being Title Suit No. 555 of 1958 against the said previous owner for declaration of this title in the suit land and the suit was decreed on 15.7.59 and then the plaintiff Tufan Das got his name recorded in the khatian and paid rent and taxes as usual and thus the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land. That the defendant opposite party No. 1 is the younger brother of the plaintiff and that the defendant had no house of his own in the town and on his prayer, the plaintiff allowed the defendant to stay in the northern bhiti Gulpata hut measuring 8 x 5 Banga in 1976 and since then the defendant has been residing therein temporarily in the suit hut. That subsequently plaintiff petitioner wanted to make a pucca construction on his own land and for that purpose the plaintiff asked the defendant opposite party to vacate his Gulpata hut but that the defendant refused to vacate the hut and, as such, the plaintiff-petitioner instituted the aforesaid title suit for khas possession. 

 9. By a perusal of the impugned judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge, it appears that the plaintiff petitioner's case is that he alone took settlement of 0.09 decimal of land of plot No. 1533 of CS Khatian No. 859 from the original owner Kiran Bala Das and others in 1359 BS but defendant opposite party's case, on the other hand, was that Kiran and others granted settlement of this 0.09 decimal of land to both Tufan Das and Kala Chand Das in 13th Falgoon 1359 BS but that none of the parties filed any paper to show the claim of the respective settlement. From this fact it appears that the alleged settlement was an oral settlement and, as such, that was a matter for decision by oral evidence. 

 11. Mr. Shamsul Alam, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioners, submits that the plaintiff-petitioner subsequently filed a Title Suit No. 555 of 1958 against the original owner and got the decree and then got his name recorded in SA Khatian by filing Misc. Case under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and then paid rent to the Government regularly and that all these papers have been marked as exhibits in the suit but that the learned courts below did not consider these facts of the case.
